clue.text: Make, say, woolly slip with hard string backing worn by elderly?

indicators.note: the outer pieces are worn, as clothing, by the inner phrase, so they wrap around it
backing means the pair of pieces is read from the end towards the start

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
cord is a length of string
past it means too old to cope, elderly

explanation.surface: A knitter's mistake in a wool garment, with a hard string stitched in behind, worn by an old person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' turns H + CORD into DROCH, and 'worn by' wraps that around PAST IT. The definition is an example: making a woolly is knitting, and a slip there is a dropped loop.
explanation.definitionFit: When knitting a woolly, letting a loop fall off the needle is the classic slip, so this is a knitting mistake.

clue.text: Range of capital announced

indicators.note: announced means the capital's name is spoken out, so we want a word sounding like it

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Some range or spread belonging to a capital city is publicly declared.
explanation.definitionFit: To range is to wander freely over an area, the verb sense shared by the answer.

clue.text: Quiet river or mere

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
the Ure is a river in Yorkshire

explanation.surface: A calm river, or a lake: mere is also a word for a small lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mere' looks like a lake to go with the river; it is the adjective, as in 'pure chance', 'mere chance'.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean nothing more than, sheer: pure luck is mere luck.

clue.text: Caught in rising black slimy fluid, die

indicators.note: in means the caught letter is placed inside the other pieces
rising, in a down clue, means the black and slimy fluid pieces are read upwards, backwards

parts.note: B is the pencil abbreviation for black
mucus is slimy fluid from the body
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Something trapped in a gloomy, slimy liquid welling up, and then dying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns B + MUCUS into SUCUMB; 'in' then puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To succumb is to give way, and in particular to die of an illness or injury.

clue.text: Reverend Barham losing medals near the house in Scotland

indicators.note: losing means the medals are taken out of the pen name

parts.note: the Rev Richard Barham wrote The Ingoldsby Legends under the pen name Thomas Ingoldsby
golds are first-place medals

explanation.surface: A Victorian clergyman stripped of his decorations, living close to a Scottish home.
explanation.walkthrough: Barham's pen name INGOLDSBY loses GOLDS. The answer is a Scots word, mostly used of farm land close to the steading.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, inby describes land or places lying close to the farmhouse, as opposed to outby.

clue.text: Wolves et al. are able to identify hollow advantage

parts.note: can means are able
ID is short for identify or identification

indicators.note: hollow means the word advantage is emptied, leaving only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Wolves and their kind can spot an empty edge over rivals.
explanation.definitionFit: Canidae is the zoological family of dogs, including wolves, foxes and jackals.

clue.text: Garland with certain fit that's worn casually

parts.note: a lei is a Hawaiian garland of flowers
sure means certain
to suit is to fit or be right for

explanation.surface: A flower garland paired with an outfit guaranteed to fit, for informal wear.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisure suit is a casual matching jacket and trousers outfit, popular in the 1970s, for relaxed wear.

clue.text: Excluding huge vacuous items in copy

parts.note: OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize, huge

indicators.note: in means the emptied items go inside the word for copy

parts.note: a tracing is a copy made through thin paper

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word items keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Leaving out enormous, empty things when making a copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Ostracising someone is shutting them out of a group, which is excluding them.

clue.text: Characters, by God, swapping sides in underworld

indicators.note: the sides of the word underworld are its outside letters, and swapping them in the god's name means one of those letters is exchanged for the other

parts.note: Zeus is the king of the Greek gods

explanation.surface: Mythic figures, swearing by a god, changing allegiance in the realm of the dead.
explanation.walkthrough: The sides of UnderworlD are U and D: ZEUS has its U swapped for D.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeds are the letter Z, so they are characters of the alphabet.

clue.text: Bernard Crick dressed without right tie

indicators.note: dressed means the letters of the name are arranged anew, as stones are dressed
without means one letter is left out of the name before rearranging

explanation.surface: The political theorist Bernard Crick got dressed but forgot his tie on the right.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop an R from BERNARD CRICK and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A carrick bend is a sailor's knot joining two ropes, and a knot is a tie.

clue.text: Urban site regularly lying about despot

indicators.note: lying about means the letters picked are turned round, read back to front
regularly means every other letter of urban site is taken, here the even ones

explanation.surface: A town location that habitually lies about a tyrant.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of uRbAn SiTe give RAST, and 'lying about' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the absolute ruler of Russia, a byword for an autocrat.

clue.text: Removed from article — rotten flesh in stock

parts.note: off means removed, as in the lid is off
the is the definite article

indicators.note: rotten means the letters of flesh have gone bad, rearranged

explanation.surface: A butcher takes decaying meat out of a joint or out of the stock on display.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods bought off the shelf are ready-made and available from stock, not made to order.

clue.text: Careless host with pets that interrupt Springwatch?

indicators.note: careless means the letters of host and pets are thrown together loosely and rearranged

parts.note: Chambers gives how as a sense of that, as in 'he told me how he had seen it'

explanation.surface: A sloppy presenter whose pets keep disrupting a BBC wildlife programme.
explanation.walkthrough: The rare sense of 'that' is a Chambers one. Springwatch is a BBC nature series, so the question mark marks it as one example of a show.
explanation.definitionFit: To stop the show is to win such applause that the performance halts, here punned as literally interrupting a programme.

clue.text: In which you'd sort out weighty issue?

definitions.text: In which you'd sort out weighty issue?

parts.words: In which you'd sort out weighty issue?
parts.note: a weighty issue here is being overweight, which a residential slimming holiday sets out to fix

explanation.walkthrough: 'weighty issue' reads as a serious problem; here it is literally excess weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential programme where overweight people go to diet and exercise, often for children.

clue.text: Conspiracy covering up international test programme?

indicators.note: covering up means the conspiracy wraps around and hides the international letter

parts.note: a plot is a conspiracy

explanation.surface: A plot to conceal an international trial scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a trial episode of a television series, made to test whether it will work.

clue.text: Obvious Romeo uncovered nice ornamented belt

parts.note: bald means plain or obvious, as in a bald statement
Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: uncovered means the outer letters of nice are stripped off, leaving its middle

explanation.surface: A plain-speaking lover strips off a pleasant decorated belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A baldric is a decorated sash or belt worn over one shoulder to carry a sword or bugle.

clue.text: Outspoken bank

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an adjective for frank, blunt and outspoken
second meaning: a steep cliff or bank

explanation.walkthrough: The words read as a bank that speaks its mind; they are two separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both an adjective for a hearty, frank manner and a noun for a steep headland or riverbank.

clue.text: Stomach ill temper about British

indicators.note: about means the ill temper surrounds the British letter

parts.note: bile means bad temper, from the old belief in bodily humours

explanation.surface: An upset gut and bad temper over something British.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stomach' looks like a verb meaning tolerate; it is the noun, a ruminant's third stomach, also called the omasum.
explanation.definitionFit: Butchers call the omasum, a cow's third stomach with leaf-like folds, the bible, after its pages.

clue.text: Error suppressed by City Police

indicators.note: suppressed by means the answer is held down inside the words city police

explanation.surface: A mistake that the urban police force has hushed up.
explanation.definitionFit: A typo is a small typing or printing slip, a kind of mistake.

clue.text: Foundation sacking bishop the way things stand

indicators.note: sacking means the bishop is dismissed from the foundation word

parts.note: a basis is a foundation
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A church foundation sacks its bishop and leaves things as they are.
explanation.definitionFit: Sold as is means sold in the present condition, the state things are in now.

clue.text: Clangers travel in space, primarily

parts.note: to go is to travel
of can mean in, as in 'of an evening' meaning in the evening

indicators.note: primarily means only the first letter of space is used

explanation.surface: The Clangers, knitted creatures of a classic British children's TV show, journeying through space.
explanation.walkthrough: The Clangers were a 1960s British children's programme about creatures on a little moon, so the surface fits; the definition is the other sense, blunders.
explanation.definitionFit: A clanger is a British slang word for a blatant mistake, as is a goof.

clue.text: Good call about, initially, stretching tight thong

indicators.note: about means the good and call pieces go around the initial letters

parts.note: to ring is to call on the phone

indicators.note: initially means the first letters of stretching and tight are taken

explanation.surface: A good phone call about stretching a snug piece of underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A G-string is a skimpy garment of a pouch on a string, a kind of thong.

clue.text: Hellish cat is an oddball

indicators.note: oddball suggests the letters of cat is an are made strange, rearranged

explanation.surface: A cat from hell is an eccentric.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means of or like Satan, the devil, so fiendish and infernal.

clue.text: Use up house-tax breaks, missing nothing

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of house-tax are broken up and rearranged
missing means a nought is left out of the letters before they are rearranged

parts.note: O, the round digit zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Tax relief on housing is spent with nothing left out.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the O from HOUSE-TAX and rearrange what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust a supply is to consume all of it, leaving none.

clue.text: Rebellious group, perhaps half having run away

indicators.note: having run away means the run letter is taken out of the word

parts.note: a half is an example of a fraction, signalled by perhaps
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A splinter group of protesters, maybe half of them, have fled.
explanation.definitionFit: A faction is a dissenting or breakaway clique within a larger body, so a group in revolt.

clue.text: Mess remains behind hotel

indicators.note: behind means the remains come after the hotel letter

parts.note: Hotel is H in the NATO phonetic alphabet
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: A messy heap of rubbish left at the back of a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a hash of something is to botch it, so a hash is a muddle.

clue.text: Facetiously opposed to calling someone when naked

indicators.note: naked means the word for calling someone is stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: paging someone is calling for them over a public address system or pager

explanation.surface: Jokingly objecting to summoning a person who has no clothes on.
explanation.definitionFit: Agin is a dialect or jocular form of against, used humorously for opposed.

clue.text: Fold up web address following fine

indicators.note: following means the web address comes after the fine letter

parts.note: F is the pencil-grading abbreviation for fine
a URL is the address of a web page

explanation.surface: Packing away a website link after being fined.
explanation.definitionFit: To furl a sail, flag or umbrella is to roll or wrap it up neatly.

clue.text: Heads of select European judiciary meeting Polish assembly

indicators.note: heads of means the first letter of each of the next four words is taken

explanation.surface: Leaders of a chosen European court meet Poland's parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sejm is the lower house of the Polish parliament, its legislative chamber.

clue.text: Monarch once quivering, angry with English knight

indicators.note: angry suggests the letters of quivering are in turmoil and rearranged

parts.note: N is the chess notation for knight

explanation.surface: A former ruler trembling with rage at an English knight.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition points to Elizabeth I, who never married.
explanation.definitionFit: Elizabeth I, England's unmarried sixteenth-century queen, was known as the Virgin Queen.

clue.text: Face King John after exchange

indicators.note: after exchange means the two words King and John swap places in the answer

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: Confronting King John following a trade or argument.
explanation.walkthrough: King John was an English monarch; swapping the order gives John then King, a toilet and K.
explanation.definitionFit: Look and face both mean a person's expression or appearance, as in a sour look.

clue.text: Press part that's tender, offering pain relief?

definitions.text: Press part that's tender, offering pain relief?

parts.words: Press part that's tender, offering pain relief?
parts.note: press is the newspapers, and the part offers advice to readers with painful personal troubles

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like pressing a sore spot for a medical cure; press is the newspapers.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's agony column prints readers' personal problems with an agony aunt's advice in reply.
